author: BroodEmperor
quote:
It's disappointing and far from what initially drew me to the Dragon Age series. This is the final straw; I won't be buying any more Bioware games, as it’s been one letdown after another.

This doesn’t feel like an RPG—it's more like a babysitter simulator, with the game holding your hand through excessive dialogue which is immersion breaking. If you're looking for an immersive RPG experience, try Cyberpunk, Baldur's Gate 3, or Dragon's Dogma 2 instead.

I'd recommend watch others' game play video first before deciding to waste your money like me.

author: BroodEmperor
quote:
Western RPGs have generally excelled over JRPGs in creating open-world, sandbox experiences. However, this DLC doesn't live up to expectations as people sees in Cyberpunk's Phantom Liberty DLC in terms of open-world RPG elements and immersive lore, or space flight mechanics when compared to something like No Man's Sky expansions. 
Even Fallout 4's DLCs surpass it. Additionally, since the choices you make don't significantly affect the endings, you're probably better off spending your time on RPGs with stronger stories, like those found in the JRPG genre.

author: BroodEmperor
quote: The game is riddled with poorly designed, unappealing characters, and plagued by bugs and lack of optimization. The gameplay is so restricted and uninspired that even Genshin Impact—a free gacha game—offers a superior experience, with greater freedom, engaging characters, and more polished mechanics. To call this game "Outlaw" is misleading when it fails to deliver on the promise of allowing players to engage in true outlaw activities.

author: BroodEmperor
quote:
The game is a remarkable achievement, especially considering it's the first AAA title from a new studio in the industry—and from China, no less.

As someone of Chinese ethnicity from Singapore, I'm deeply familiar with Journey to the West and the Monkey King, and this game hits all the right notes for me. It features excellent game mechanics, stunning graphics, and impressive animations at the end of each chapter. The story, dialogue, and attention to detail, with no reused assets—unlike some other AAA studios—really stand out. I encountered almost no bugs, which is rare.

I'm excited to see what other elements of Chinese mythology and folklore they will explore in their next game!

author: BroodEmperor
quote:
DO NOT EXPECT TREAT THIS AS A SPACE SIM!

And get rid of the false advertisement, marketing that Bethesda sold you like "unprecedented freedom" to explore a thousand planets, that "We are putting you in the cockpit of your very own spaceship and telling you that you can do pretty much anything." (Actually just loading screens when we are traveling unless you gonna spend hours flying), that "Space flight should be EXCITING and dangerous, and you should feel like you're in COMPLETE CONTROL EVERY STEP OF THE WAY. " (Couple of loading screens per travel between planets shows that I am FULLY in control.) and that you could visit any area of a planet and so on. The game is a good game for sure, but Bethesda is at fault for marketing and overhyping it.

I do agree it's frustrating with the way they marketed it and they should not have worded it that way. If you are a fellow lover of No Man's Sky, Elite Dangerous, or any other space sim games, you will be disappointed. Instead, treat this as a RPG set in Space faring/exploration era with limited open world capabilities (like a bigger Fallout 4 open world map being dissected and separated into different planets with a limited space for you to explore) and the core focus on individual rpg elements, dialogues and story.

Starfield is a fun game when you slowly get into it no doubt, but being a Bethesda game, as with most of their games, there are bugs and glitches, not as much as previous fallout games, but definitely still there. My first 5 hours or so was bug free, but I started seeing NPCs spasming and clipping through the assets like walls/floors or floating up into unreachable heights once I got into the Constellation first main mission...Maybe that's how the human body works when you stay in space too long. Trust Bethesda on this, they studied it. So as a Bethesda game, forget other non-vanilla in game contents like modders created costumes, etc, you got to use performance/ optimization mods to optimize and make you game work much more smoothly, have better fps and look better.

All in all, the game is fun at the first few hours if you are someone who love RPGs and the thing is with Bethesda games, they are selling a foundation, am unpolished game for modders and for players to apply mods to on top of it. It's a 5/10 for the vanilla game by Bethesda, but you will use mods to make it into a 10/10 by modders hand provided modders even want to make mods for this game.
